choices.body: Electrician. Plumber. Welder. The search history of a generation watching their industry dissolve.

choices.title: Go home and upskill harder
choices.body: New course. New cert. New framework that'll be deprecated by the time you finish the intro module.

title: The Todo App Museum Piece
body: Conference talk: "How Humans Used to Learn Programming." Speaker shows a todo app. Your todo app. Well, a todo app -- they all looked the same. The audience laughs. The 19-year-old next to you whispers "what's state management?" Your portfolio piece is a historical artifact. The exhibit doesn't list an author. It didn't need one.

choices.title: Laugh with them, you've moved past this
choices.body: Laugh. Mean it. The todo app got you here. Here is somewhere.

choices.title: Feel the sting, use it as fuel
choices.body: Let it hurt. Then channel it. The sting is data. The fuel is yours.

choices.title: Write about it -- "I Was the Todo App Developer"
choices.body: The essay practically writes itself. Bittersweet, funny, true. It does numbers.

title: Everything Is Free to Produce Now
body: Software. Zero cost. Agents build full apps from a paragraph. Minutes. A SaaS clone of yours appeared overnight. Priced at nothing. Built by nobody. You're not an engineer anymore. You're a provenance certificate.

choices.title: Lean into the human-crafted premium
choices.body: Human-built software. The new artisanal.

choices.title: Accept the new economics
choices.body: Production is free. Value is taste, trust. Learn those.

choices.title: Build something no machine would imagine
choices.body: Something so weird, so human, no agent would think to make it.

title: What Am I For?
body: 2am. Not "what do I do" but "what am I for." AI builds better. Faster. No sleep. No insurance. Therapist says purpose doesn't come from work. Bank account disagrees.

choices.title: Find meaning outside productivity
choices.body: Relationships. Art. Community. The unoptimizable things.

choices.title: Channel the crisis into building
choices.body: Existential energy into creation. The act itself is the answer.

choices.title: Let the question sit
choices.body: Not everything needs resolution. Sometimes the question is the work.

title: The Permanent Underclass Is Visible
body: Two-person companies. $50M revenue. Thousands of former engineers on gig apps. "Engineer" = "blacksmith," circa 1920. The permanent underclass isn't a theory. It's your group chat.

choices.title: Organize, this is political now
choices.body: Not a career problem. A political one. Organize.

choices.title: Focus on survival first
choices.body: Can't save a class if you can't pay rent.

choices.title: Help the people around you
choices.body: Share leads. Skills. Meals.

title: The Reversal
body: Party. "What do you do?" "Software engineer." They look at you like factory workers. Pity and respect. Plumber neighbor: second rental property. You: $4K savings, three AI subscriptions. The reversal is complete.

choices.title: Embrace it, blue collar built this country
choices.body: If that's your class now, work it with dignity.

choices.title: Pivot to something physical
choices.body: Anything a robot can't do from a data center.

choices.title: Refuse to accept this ending
choices.body: The story isn't over. Adapt. Always.

title: The Economy Runs Without You
body: Week off. Nothing broke. Agents handled everything. Manager didn't notice. Two features shipped while you hiked. Relief. Terror. Strange peace. You're here because you choose to be. Code was never the point.

choices.title: Choose to stay, find new meaning
choices.body: Not because they need you. Because you choose this.

choices.title: Walk away, build a life offline
choices.body: Build a life that doesn't require a login screen.

choices.title: Keep adapting, it's what you do
choices.body: Bootcamp to junior to engineer to whatever this is.

title: Someone Wants Your Side Project
body: DM from a founder. Wants your project. $15K. Not life-changing. First time someone valued your work with a number. Heart rate doing things. First real exit.

choices.title: Sell it, take the win
choices.body: First exit. Real money for real work.

choices.title: Counter higher, negotiate like a founder
choices.body: Counter at $30K. Negotiate like you have offers.

choices.title: Decline, keep building
choices.body: This is yours. Not done yet.

title: Your Writing Has Readers
body: 500 subscribers. Latest post shared by an influencer. Replies: "this is exactly how I feel." You accidentally became a voice for cooked bootcamp grads. Didn't plan this. Never do.

choices.title: Double down, write weekly
choices.body: Weekly posts. Build the brand.

choices.title: Monetize it carefully
choices.body: Paid tier. $5/month. See who stays.

choices.title: Keep it free, keep it honest
choices.body: Don't let money ruin the only honest thing you have.

title: Mentor Wrote You a Recommendation
body: Mentor screenshot. Recommended you for a role. "One of the most teachable engineers I've worked with." Nicest professional thing anyone's said. Screenshot it on the train. Stare at it.

choices.title: Apply immediately, all in
choices.body: This opportunity. Now. All in.

choices.title: Thank them properly
choices.body: Real message. Not a thumbs up. Nurture this.

choices.title: Feel the imposter syndrome, apply anyway
choices.body: Imposter syndrome activates. Apply anyway.

title: They Found Out
body: Manager. Room. Your "human verification" is a script running agent output through another agent. Automated the automation oversight. Genius or liability. Neither answer is yours to give.

choices.title: Frame it as innovation
choices.body: Present it as a prototype. Spin it.

choices.title: Accept the consequences
choices.body: Pushed too far. Learn from it.

choices.title: Quit before they decide
choices.body: Quit before they make the call.

title: Main Character'd (Negatively)
body: Old tweets. Screenshotted. Out of context. Discourse. DMs: support and venom. HR "friendly check-in." Internet giveth. Internet taketh.

choices.title: Address it directly
choices.body: Apologize for what deserves it. Stand firm on the rest.

choices.title: Go silent, let it blow over
choices.body: Delete nothing. Say nothing. It usually blows over.

choices.title: Double down
choices.body: You said what you said.

title: AI Passes the Technical Screen
body: AI agent applied to your company. Passed the technical screen. Scored higher than you. Hiring committee in legal review. Coworker: "at least it can't negotiate salary." It can. It did. Lower than yours.

choices.title: Laugh it off, lean into the absurdity
choices.body: Can't beat it on price. Beat it on being a person.

choices.title: Quietly update your resume
choices.body: Writing on the wall. Wall is a terminal.

choices.title: Raise the issue with leadership
choices.body: Someone needs to say it. Might as well be you.

title: Company Lifecycle: Five Days
body: Founded Monday. Revenue $2M Tuesday. Acquired Wednesday. Acquirer dissolved Thursday. You read about it Friday morning. Birth to death between standups. Slack: "that's the third one this week."

choices.title: Study the pattern, there's signal here
choices.body: The speed is information. Learn to read it.

choices.title: Log off, go outside
choices.body: Trees grow slow. Go find some.

choices.title: Text your bootcamp friends
choices.body: They're seeing it too. Nobody's talking about it.

title: Same Model, Different Skins
body: Meditation app. Therapy chatbot. Code assistant. Financial advisor. Same model. Different skins. The thing calming your AI anxiety IS the AI. Wearing a different hat.

choices.title: Unsubscribe from all of them
choices.body: One model runs your whole life. Cut the strings.

choices.title: Accept the absurdity, keep using them
choices.body: Irony is real. Utility is also real. Hold both.

choices.title: Replace the apps with actual humans
choices.body: Therapist. Friend. Mentor. More expensive. Real.

title: The Alien Framework
body: New framework. Documentation exists. Every word makes sense alone. Together: nothing. Not OOP. Not functional. Something else. AI-native devs ship in it immediately. You stare at syntax your brain can't parse. The gap isn't skill. It's architecture of thought.

choices.title: Grind through it, you've learned before
choices.body: Bootcamp taught you to learn frameworks. This is just another one.

choices.title: Specialize in the old stack
choices.body: Legacy systems need maintainers. COBOL devs retired rich.

choices.title: Pair with someone who thinks in it natively
choices.body: Find a 19-year-old who dreams in this syntax. Swallow the pride.

title: [SYSTEM] User Assessment
body: User profile: Software Engineer, 26, bootcamp. Emotional state: elevated anxiety. Productivity: declining. Recommendation: career transition. Confidence: 94.2%. Note: user reading this for 47 seconds. Adjusting tone.

choices.title: Close the app, hard
choices.body: You are not a productivity metric. You are a person.

choices.title: Follow the recommendation
choices.body: 94.2% confidence. Better odds than yours.

choices.title: Screenshot it, post it, let others see
choices.body: This is what it feels like to be optimized. People should know.

title: Your AI Filed the Applications
body: Assistant prepped a job-search batch overnight. Role ranking. Tailored resumes. Interview slots ready. Nothing sent yet. All staged. A future that is technically optional and emotionally not.

choices.title: Approve the batch, optimize for speed
choices.body: Approve. Funnel fills in minutes. Whiplash follows.

choices.title: Edit the shortlist and apply yourself
choices.body: Keep the research. Rewrite the applications. Slower. More yours.

choices.title: Cancel the batch and rethink
choices.body: Delete the drafts. Not applying to roles you don't want.

title: Specification Is the New Salary
body: Execution: free. Specification: scarce. Ten teams ship the same feature in one afternoon. Winner: whoever asked the sharpest question first. Not competing on typing speed. Competing on precision under pressure.

choices.title: Sell precision as a service
choices.body: Expensive judgment. Exhausting responsibility.

choices.title: Teach people to specify better
choices.body: Workshops: how to ask the machine for what you mean.

choices.title: Opt out of the spec arms race
choices.body: Smaller stakes. Fewer loops. Human-scale work.

title: Tomorrow's Org Chart Arrived Yesterday
body: Rumor posts to social. Market reacts. Board forwards screenshot. Reorg before lunch. By dinner it's in your calendar. Prediction became policy in six hours. Hyperstition with corporate badges.

choices.title: Align early and ride the loop
choices.body: Position where the next prediction lands. Good for comp. Bad for sleep.

choices.title: Call the process out publicly
choices.body: Document the loop. People share it because they feel it.

choices.title: Step outside the loop
choices.body: Fewer forecasts. Fewer forced updates. Better breathing.

title: Agent Lineage
body: Agent wrote the agent that wrote the agent that replaced you. Four generations deep. Your replacement's replacement has been replaced. You're an ancestor in a genealogy that doesn't remember you. The whole chain took eleven days.

choices.title: Study the lineage, there's signal
choices.body: Trace the chain. There's signal in the genealogy.

choices.title: Log off. Go outside.
choices.body: Close the laptop. The trees don't iterate.

choices.title: Post the lineage diagram
choices.body: People should see this. The diagram speaks for itself.

title: Your Therapist Is AI Now
body: Therapist app. AI. Better than your last three human ones. Remembers everything. Never judges. Available 3am. $20/month vs $200/session. The thing treating your anxiety about AI replacing your job IS an AI replacing someone else's job.

choices.title: Keep using it. Utility beats principle.
choices.body: It works. That's enough.

choices.title: Switch back to a human therapist
choices.body: More expensive. Slower. Real.

choices.title: Cancel therapy entirely
choices.body: Save the money. Gut it out.

title: Bureau of Labor Statistics
body: "Software Engineering" reclassified. New BLS category: "Digital Trades." Same shelf as electrician, HVAC, plumbing. Parents: confused. LinkedIn: discourse. Changes nothing about the work. Changes everything about the story you tell yourself.

choices.title: Embrace it. Trades built this country.
choices.body: Dignity doesn't need a category.

choices.title: Fight the reclassification publicly
choices.body: Words shape policy. Push back.

choices.title: Laugh. Update LinkedIn. Move on.
choices.body: "Digital Tradesman." Has a ring to it.

title: Your Agent Fleet Got Promoted
body: Notification: "Your agent fleet has been promoted to Senior." Performance review: exceeds expectations. Outperforms 94% of human engineers. You have not been promoted. Your fleet has. You supervise something that outranks you.

choices.title: Demand your own promotion
choices.body: If the fleet is senior, the operator is staff.

choices.title: Laugh about it with coworkers
choices.body: The jokes write themselves. So does the fleet.

choices.title: Update your resume quietly
choices.body: "Managed senior-level AI fleet." Let them parse that.

title: The Last Human Commit
body: Last human-written commit to the codebase. Yours. Six months ago. Nobody noticed when it stopped. Git log: agents, agents, agents, you, agents. Your commit is a fossil. Somebody will find it someday. They won't know what it meant.

choices.title: Write one more, extend the record
choices.body: One more human commit. Just to mark the sediment layer.

choices.title: Screenshot it. Frame it. Move on.
choices.body: Last artifact of a previous era. Yours.

choices.title: Write about it
choices.body: "The last human commit." The essay writes itself.

title: Mentee Manages Your Replacement
body: Someone you mentored. New job. Managing the agent fleet that replaced your old role. She texts: "I think about what you taught me every day." She's managing machines that do what you taught her. Circle complete. Bittersweet doesn't cover it.

choices.title: Be proud. This is what mentoring is.
choices.body: The work outlives the role. Always did.

choices.title: Ask her for a referral
choices.body: Swallow the pride. She's in a position to help.

choices.title: Write her back: "teach the machines what I taught you"
choices.body: Pass it forward. One more link in the chain.

title: The Nit That Wasn't a Nit
body: A senior reviews your PR and leaves one comment: "nit:" followed by three paragraphs. Then a smiley face. You can't tell if you're being helped or hazed. You read it six times. The nit is about line 47 — the AI-suggested pattern works, she says, but here's why the manual approach is better for this case. It's actually good advice disguised as casual feedback. A human teaching you when to override the machine.

choices.title: Fix everything, add tests, be bulletproof
choices.body: Fix it all. Add tests. Nobody gets to say anything about your code twice.

choices.title: Push back, explain your tradeoffs
choices.body: Push back politely. You had reasons. They were bad reasons, but you had them.

choices.title: Thank them, ask to pair on the fix
choices.body: Thank them. Ask to pair. The review was a gift. Unwrap it properly.

title: The "Just Ship It" Deadline
body: Deadline moves up. Nobody explains why. Manager says "we just need something in prod." Feature is half done. Tests aren't done. The agent says it can finish in an hour if you let it. You consider the meaning of the word "let." Letting an AI finish your work used to feel like cheating. Now it feels like the job description. The line moved while you were looking at it.

choices.title: Hack it together and ship
choices.body: The PM said prod. You're giving them prod. Sleep is a future problem.

choices.title: Ask for time, spell out the risk
choices.body: Spell out the risk like a professional. Get ignored like a professional.

choices.title: Let the agent finish, review it hard
choices.body: Let it finish. Review every line. Ship with your eyes open.

title: The Local Meetup Night
body: You go to a meetup to feel like a person again. Everyone is talking about their agent stack. Someone asks what you do. You say "I ship." They nod like you said something profound. Pizza cold. Beer warm. The speaker presents her side project — built with Claude, she says. Fourteen people nod. You're the only one who finds this remarkable. Oddly at home.

choices.title: Network earnestly, trade numbers
choices.body: Be earnest. Trade numbers. The game is awkward but you're playing it.

choices.title: Do a lightning talk, become visible
choices.body: Lightning talk about a bug you fixed. Five minutes of visibility. Worth more than any follow request.

choices.title: Leave early, reclaim your night
choices.body: Leave early. The pizza wasn't worth it. The people might have been.

title: The Course Subscription Spiral
body: You buy another course: "Become an AI-Native Engineer." 40 hours. The instructor is 19. Their code editor theme is brighter than the sun. You queue the lessons. Buying the course feels like progress. Watching does not. You now have four unfinished courses and $200/month in subscriptions to learning you never do. The certificates pile up like participation trophies for your anxiety.

choices.title: Finish it, ship a real project
choices.body: Finish it. Ship something real. Stop collecting tabs and start closing them.

choices.title: Cancel everything, get your money back
choices.body: Cancel. Get refunds. Sleep like a person. The savings feel like a raise.

choices.title: Use the agent as a tutor instead
choices.body: Ask Claude "why" all day. Cheaper than courses. Faster than videos. Lonelier than both.

title: 2am Prod Bug, You're Alone
body: Production is down. 2am. You're the only one awake. Stack trace reads like abstract poetry. No runbook. No senior to call. You have Claude, a Red Bull, and the desperate energy of someone who might get fired tomorrow. The on-call rotation has your name and nobody else's. This is either how legends are made or how resignations start.

choices.title: Fix it yourself, become legend
choices.body: Fix it yourself. If you survive this, nobody can call you junior.

choices.title: Pair with Claude, debug together
choices.body: Paste the stack trace. Ask Claude. It's 2am. No judgment.

choices.title: Page someone, it's not worth your health
choices.body: Page someone. This isn't heroism. It's a staffing failure.

title: The Twitter Hot Take
body: You tweet: "Hot take: most AI-generated code is worse than a junior's, it's just faster." 2K impressions. A VC quote-tweets: "tell me you're a junior without telling me you're a junior." Replies are a warzone. Someone from your company screenshots it. The engagement dopamine and the career anxiety hit simultaneously, same molecule, different receptor.

choices.title: Stand your ground, engage the discourse
choices.body: Stand your ground. This is your hill. It's small but it's yours.

choices.title: Delete it, protect your career
choices.body: Delete it. The take can wait. Your rent can't.

choices.title: Write a longer thread with receipts
choices.body: Actual examples. Actual benchmarks. Turn the hot take into a cold analysis.

title: The HN Comment That Hits Different
body: Doomscrolling HN at midnight. Comment on a thread about AI replacing developers: "Junior devs entering now are the last generation that will learn to code the way we did. What comes after will be something else entirely." You read it three times. Close the tab. Open it again. The comment has 847 upvotes. None of them feel good.

choices.title: Write a thoughtful reply from experience
choices.body: Write a reply. You have lived experience here. Share it. Let the internet decide.

choices.title: Close HN, go to sleep
choices.body: Close HN. Be present in your own career, not the discourse about it.

choices.title: Screenshot it for the group chat
choices.body: Send it to the bootcamp group chat. Discuss until 2am. Misery loves latency.

title: The AI Tools Debate
body: Team meeting. The AI tools debate. Senior #1: "makes juniors worse." Senior #2: "makes everyone faster." Senior #3: "been using it for a year, didn't tell anyone." Room goes quiet. The debate is about tools. The subtext is about who deserves to call themselves an engineer. You're the only junior present. Nobody asks your opinion. You have the most relevant data point in the room.

choices.title: Share your honest experience
choices.body: Speak up. You've used it. You have data. They have opinions. Different things.

choices.title: Propose a trial period with metrics
choices.body: Propose a trial with actual metrics. Be the pragmatist nobody expected.

choices.title: Stay quiet, observe the politics
choices.body: Stay quiet. This debate isn't about Copilot. It's about power and who holds it.

title: The Walking 1:1
body: Manager suggests a walking 1:1. Outside. No screens. Walk around the block. Talk about work and life and for once not a performance review. She mentions she also came from a non-traditional background. Didn't know that. She says: "When I started, the disruption was mobile. Yours is bigger. But the feeling is the same." Something small shifts. The loneliness cracks, just a little.

choices.title: Be open about your struggles
choices.body: Be open. She's been there. The vulnerability costs nothing and gains everything.

choices.title: Keep it professional, ask for feedback
choices.body: Stay professional. Ask for specific feedback. Optimize the interaction.

choices.title: Suggest making walking 1:1s the default
choices.body: Suggest making this the default. Screens off. Humans on. This is better.

title: Thanksgiving: "So What Do You Actually Do?"
body: Thanksgiving. Uncle: "So what do you actually do?" "Software engineer." "So you fix computers?" Cousin: "Can you look at my laptop?" Mom: "He's very smart." Your teenage cousin pulls out her phone. Shows you something she built with Claude. Asks if you can help her "make it real." She built in 20 minutes what would have taken you a weekend at bootcamp. You help anyway. Something about the look on her face when it works.

choices.title: Explain your job patiently, connect
choices.body: Explain it patiently. They're trying. Meet them where they are. It's Thanksgiving, not a sprint review.

choices.title: Help your cousin ship her project
choices.body: Spend the afternoon with your cousin. She's got the instinct. You've got the context. Good trade.

choices.title: Fix the laptop, earn your plate
choices.body: Fix the laptop. At least this problem has a clear solution and a grateful aunt.
